summary: The tutor and student are discussing circle theorems, especially angles in the same segment, tangents, and radii meeting tangents at right angles.

timeline.speaker: Tutor
timeline.text: Let's start with the angle in the same segment theorem.

timeline.speaker: Student
timeline.text: So if both angles stand on the same chord they must be equal?

timeline.speaker: Tutor
timeline.text: Exactly, and remember the radius meets the tangent at ninety degrees.
timeline.summary: Tutor links tangent-radius rule into the discussion.

items.definition: A line segment joining two points on a circle.
A straight line that touches the circle at exactly one point.

widgets.title: Worked Example
widgets.problem: Two angles stand on the same chord AB. One angle is 52°. Find the other.
steps: Identify that both angles subtend the same chord.
Therefore the second angle is also 52°.

widgets.title: Common Mistakes
items: Using the theorem when the angles do not stand on the same chord.
Forgetting that tangent-radius gives a right angle.
Mixing up same-segment and alternate-segment results.

widgets.title: Quick Check
widgets.question: What angle is formed between a tangent and the radius at the point of contact?
